$comment: One short line each for the catalog. `node scripts/catalog.mjs` turns this into the tables in README.md and docs/guides/catalog.md. Every skill in plugins/ needs an entry; CI checks it.

grilling.what: The interview engine behind grill-me: relentless questions, in rounds, until the plan has no gaps.
grilling.when: You have a plan or idea and want its holes found before you build.

grill-me.what: Starts a grilling interview about whatever you describe.
grill-me.when: You want to stress-test an idea, anywhere, with no files involved.

grill-with-docs.what: Grilling that also writes down the decisions as a glossary and ADRs in your repo.
grill-with-docs.when: You're planning inside a project and want the reasoning kept.

domain-modeling.what: Builds a shared vocabulary for a project in CONTEXT.md and records decisions as ADRs.
domain-modeling.when: Words in your project mean different things to different people.

to-spec.what: Turns the conversation so far into a written spec on your issue tracker.
to-spec.when: A grilling session is done and the result should become a spec.

to-tickets.what: Splits a plan or spec into small tickets, each saying what it waits on.
to-tickets.when: Work is too big for one session and needs to be done piece by piece.

to-questionnaire.what: Turns open questions into a questionnaire someone else can fill in.
to-questionnaire.when: You can't answer a decision yourself and need input from a client or colleague.

wayfinder.what: Maps a huge, unclear project as decision tickets and resolves them one by one.
wayfinder.when: The project is so big or foggy you don't know where to start.

triage.what: Sorts incoming issues and pull requests, checks them, and writes agent-ready briefs.
triage.when: Bug reports and requests from others are piling up.

research.what: Sends a background agent to read primary sources and write the findings to a file.
research.when: You need facts from docs or APIs and don't want to wait while they're gathered.

council.what: Seven expert personas debate a question, then give a verdict with risks and next steps.
council.when: You face a decision and want it argued from very different angles.

setup-matt-pocock-skills.what: One-time setup for a repo: issue tracker, triage labels, where docs live.
setup-matt-pocock-skills.when: Before the first use of to-spec, to-tickets, triage, wayfinder or code-review in a repo.

implement.what: Builds a spec or ticket test-first, then reviews and commits it.
implement.when: A ticket or small spec is ready to be built.

implement-spec.what: Builds a whole spec with parallel sub-agents and opens one pull request.
implement-spec.when: A spec with many tickets is ready and you want it built in one go.

tdd.what: Test-driven development, one red-green step at a time.
tdd.when: You want a feature or fix built test-first.

diagnosing-bugs.what: Reproduces a hard bug with one failing command before fixing it, then adds a regression test.
diagnosing-bugs.when: Something is broken, flaky or slow and the cause isn't obvious.

code-review.what: Reviews changes on two axes: your repo's coding standards and what the spec asked for.
code-review.when: A branch or pull request is ready for review.
code-review.trigger: Automatic, or `/coding:code-review` (plain `/code-review` is Claude Code's own, different review)

codebase-design.what: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules with small interfaces.
codebase-design.when: You're deciding how to shape a module, interface or seam.

improve-codebase-architecture.what: Scans a codebase for places to simplify and shows them as a visual report.
improve-codebase-architecture.when: The code feels tangled and you want to know where to start cleaning up.

resolving-merge-conflicts.what: Resolves a merge or rebase conflict by finding out why each side changed.
resolving-merge-conflicts.when: Git stopped a merge or rebase with conflicts.

setup-pre-commit.what: Adds Husky pre-commit hooks for formatting, type checks and tests.
setup-pre-commit.when: You want checks to run automatically before every commit.

playwright-cli.what: Drives a real browser from the terminal: open pages, click, fill forms, take screenshots.
playwright-cli.when: Claude should test, inspect or automate a website. Needs `npm install -g @playwright/cli`.

wizard.what: Writes an interactive script that walks you through steps only a human can do.
wizard.when: A setup needs you to click through dashboards or paste secrets.

impeccable.what: Designs, critiques and polishes frontend interfaces, with 20+ sub-commands like audit, polish and typeset.
impeccable.when: A page or app works but doesn't look or feel right.

writing-for-agents.what: How to write skills, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files that agents follow well.
writing-for-agents.when: You're writing or editing a skill or agent instructions.

writing-fragments.what: Collects raw thoughts and fragments for a piece of writing, with no structure yet.
writing-fragments.when: You're at the start of an article and have ideas but no outline.

writing-shape.what: Shapes raw material into an article, paragraph by paragraph.
writing-shape.when: You have the material and want it turned into a finished text.

teach.what: Teaches you a concept step by step, using your own workspace as the example.
teach.when: You want to understand something, not just have it done.

wait-what.what: Makes Claude re-explain its last message in plain, simple English.

handoff.what: Writes a handoff document so a fresh session can continue the work.
handoff.when: The conversation is getting long or you'll continue another day.

claude-handoff.what: Hands the work to a new background agent that continues straight away.
claude-handoff.when: You want the work to go on in the background while you do something else.

retro.what: Runs a short retrospective on the session: what worked, what didn't, what to change.
retro.when: A piece of work is finished and you want to learn from it.

suggester.what: Turns skill suggestions on or off.
suggester.when: Suggestions get in your way, or you want them back.

task-observer.what: Watches your sessions and proposes new skills or improvements to existing ones.
task-observer.when: You build your own skills and want ideas for them collected as you work.

taste-skill.what: 14 skills for art direction: design directions, reference images, brand kits and style presets.
taste-skill.when: Generated frontends look generic and you want a distinct visual style.

ponytail.what: Lazy senior dev mode: pushes Claude to the smallest solution that works, plus audit and review commands.
ponytail.when: Claude tends to over-engineer and you want leaner code.
ponytail.trigger: Always on once installed; `/ponytail-help` for commands
